Race is widely discussed factor in policing outcomes. In this analysis we seek to explore how race of the individual stopped relate to arrest rates in traffic stops, using data from a study of New Orleans traffic stops. Arrests in the study may not reflect the totality of police actions that we care about such as summonses and detainment.


$$
P(Y = 1) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-(\beta_0 + \beta_1 X_1 + \beta_2 X_2 + \cdots + \beta_n X_n)}}
$$

with $( Y \sim \text{Bernoulli}(\rho) )$ where $( \rho = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-(\beta_0 + \beta_1 X_1 + \beta_2 X_2 + \cdots + \beta_n X_n)}} )$
